cap: The scrotal wall is the abdominal wall carried down with the testis, so each layer matches a lesson: the dartos is the plane of Fournier gangrene, the cremaster carries the cremasteric reflex, the tunica vaginalis is the sac of a hydrocele and the tunica albuginea limits swelling. The testis also keeps its retroperitoneal supply: the left testicular vein enters the left renal vein, the right enters the vena cava, and testicular lymph goes to para-aortic nodes rather than the groin.
teach: The venous asymmetry explains why varicoceles are left-sided and why a new right-sided one suggests a retroperitoneal mass. The lymphatic asymmetry explains why a testicular tumor is removed through the groin: a scrotal incision would open a second drainage route to the inguinal nodes. The penis and scrotal skin are surface structures and drain to superficial inguinal nodes, so penile cancer prognosis is set in the groin.
